source.title: Can Kernel Methods Explain How the Data Affects Neural Collapse?

record.tranche_reason: The study trains finite-width FCNs by gradient descent and measures feature-collapse metrics, with training loss and sign predictions also shown. This is related to training behavior but does not measure training classification error as the listed versions define it; its NC1 results bear on V1 only insofar as they examine networks trained beyond zero training error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training loss and sign-prediction plots for trained networks, but the reported NC1 metric is within-class feature variability relative to between-class variability, not training classification error. The direct NC1/kernel comparisons do not establish whether training classification error reaches zero. Rows below capture explicit training loss/sign prediction outcomes and the study’s stated NC1 results for trained FCNs; kernel-only NC1 findings are not rows for the claim’s error behavior.
record.test_reason: The study measures neural-collapse feature variability and kernel approximation in fully connected networks on synthetic Gaussian data. These results do not test any listed version. Training-loss and sign-prediction illustrations do not establish V1's training classification-error result for convolutional networks on CIFAR; depth experiments measure NC1, and learning-rate adjustments do not test stability thresholds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors additionally emphasize that NTK does not represent more collapsed features than NNGP on the studied Gaussian data. Adaptive kernels offer progress toward data-dependent NC analysis, but their agreement with trained networks remains incomplete; ERF yields lower NC1 than ReLU.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses two-layer FCNs trained with vanilla gradient descent to examine neural-collapse feature variability, not the benchmark training-error outcome in the claim. It also analytically and empirically evaluates NNGP, NTK, and a data-aware GP kernel.
record.method_sensitivity: Data dimension, sample size, class imbalance, linear separability, activation function, and annealing schedule affect reported NC1 behavior or kernel approximation.

fits_no_version.finding: NTK features are not more collapsed than NNGP features on the Gaussian datasets analyzed theoretically and empirically (Sections 5.3–5.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lazy-training kernels can fail to capture neural-collapse feature learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-aware GP kernels yield lower NC1 than NNGP and approximate some shallow-network trends, but disagree under class imbalance and higher-dimensional overlapping classes (Section 6.3; Appendix G).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-adaptive kernels capture some, but not all, data-dependent neural-collapse behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: ERF produces lower NC1 than ReLU in the analyzed kernels and trained networks (Section 5.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects within-class feature collapse.

record.problems: The study's central metric is NC1 rather than training classification error. Training-loss and sign-prediction outcomes are presented in figures without numerical values or a textual statement that classification error is zero. EoS solutions depend on a manually selected annealing schedule; the authors note that existence and uniqueness of solutions are not rigorously studied.
record.rows_left_out: No rows meet the required outcome measure: the numerical NC1 results do not measure training classification error, and the training-loss/sign-prediction plots do not state a numerical or explicit classification-error result.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels and size, stopping, or regularization comparisons.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies in ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Depth-related training-error degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization comparisons measuring training speed, signal or gradient propagation, or trainable depth.
Loss recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons measuring training speed or learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 designation and V1 tested_not_extracted status. The zero-training-error discussion supplies background for neural collapse, not a direct test of V1. Figure 8's loss and sign-prediction illustrations are already declared in rows_left_out; their numerical outcomes cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report numerical training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR benchmarks, model-size/error sweeps, or early stopping/regularization comparisons. Its trained FCN NC1 findings do not measure the error outcome V1 names.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
